subject: Machine Learning
error_analysis:
v2 held-out test run, 33 questions (28 answerable, 5 not in the books), Hugging Face Qwen2.5-1.5B (bfloat16). The same questions were also run with the quote-only baseline and the Ollama fast mode. Changes since v1 (chosen on the validation split, which grew from 10 to 22 questions): bge-small-en-v1.5 embeddings (256 tokens) instead of all-MiniLM-L6-v2; removal of paragraphs repeated on 20%+ of a book's pages (copyright notices, running headers, page numbers); hybrid BM25 + vector search; evidence threshold 0.67 (was 0.30, recalibrated for the new embedding model); grounding cutoff 0.4 (was 0.5); quote fallback instead of refusing when the model's wording cannot be verified.

1. Retrieval: hit rate 53.6% (unchanged from v1), recall@5 48.2% (v1 46.4%); target 80%. Validation was 80% on 20 answerable questions, so these changes did not carry over to the test split. As in v1, many misses retrieve valid pages that are not listed in expected_evidence (several books cover the same topic), and cross-book questions (Q030-Q034) still retrieve mostly one book. A cross-encoder reranker and a per-book cap were tried on validation and made results worse (75% and 70%), so they are off.

2. Abstention: 3 of 5 no-answer questions refused (v1: 5 of 5). Q035 (deploying on AWS SageMaker) was answered from D2L's appendix on renting AWS EC2 machines: the words match, so the grounding check passes a misleading answer. Q038 (new features in Python 3.13) received an unrelated quote from the quote fallback, which only needs one shared keyword. Wrongly refused answerable questions fell from 21.4% to 14.3% (Ollama mode 7.1%); the remaining ones are mostly calculations (Q025 R-squared, Q029 correlation), where the model reports insufficient evidence because the computed value does not appear in the passage.

3. Citations: 100% resolve to stored passages; cited pages match the expected pages 47.9% of the time (v1 31.8%).

4. Speed: mean 52.5 s, p95 81.5 s per answer in bfloat16 (v1 float32: 48.6 s); peak RAM 3.9 GB (v1 6.8 GB). The Ollama mode answered the same questions in 7.6 s on average (p95 11.2 s) with comparable metrics.

5. Answer model choice (validation): qwen2.5:3b in Ollama was slower (11.8 s) and wrongly refused 25% of answerable questions against 0% for qwen2.5:1.5b, so the 1.5B model is kept.

Not changed after seeing these test results, to keep the test split held out. Candidate fixes to check on the validation split first: require the quote fallback to share several question keywords with the quoted sentence; number-aware grounding that accepts values computed from numbers in the passage; one retrieval per book named in cross-book questions; and complete expected_evidence lists for topics covered in several books.
limitations: Retrieval is below the 80% target on the test split, and page-exact evidence matching undercounts valid pages from other books. The lexical grounding check compares words, not meaning: it can pass an on-topic but misleading answer (Q035) and reject computed numbers. The quote fallback can quote loosely related text. The 1.5B models rarely carry out calculations. Hugging Face answers take about 50-80 s on this CPU-only laptop; the Ollama mode takes about 7 s but uses a 4-bit quantized copy of the model. Evaluation questions and reference answers are drafts and still need subject-expert review. Books 014 and 015 are commercial and their permission is not confirmed. Passages never cross page boundaries; equations and tables lose layout.
